verdict.rationale: Gumloop documents event-driven automation for agents: app triggers fire when something happens in an external service, and webhook triggers give an agent a URL that runs it when another system POSTs data. The evidence does not show user-defined rules (conditions, filters, or if-this-then-that logic) that decide which events trigger which actions; the trigger simply launches an agent, which then reasons about what to do. missing for 10: documented rule or condition definition on triggers (event filters, per-event action mapping), detail on which app events are supported, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: app triggers to fire when something happens in an external service
A webhook trigger gives an agent its own URL. Anything that can send an HTTP POST — Stripe, GitHub, a cron job, an internal script — runs the agent by calling it.
Build AI agents that use your tools and data to do real work, then automate them with triggers, schedules, and the API.
